title: How do we cut a square grid into odd numbers of dots?
description: A square grid of thirty six dots is cut into corner layers of one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven dots. Keeko's doubt, that the grid is cut into equal rows, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square grid is cut into L shaped layers from one corner, and each layer has two more dots than the one inside it. Watch for students who cut the grid into equal rows.

source: How can we partition the dots in a square grid into odd numb
video_script.why: The child cuts a square grid of dots into L shaped layers that hold one, three, five and more dots, and sees that each layer has two more dots than the one inside it.
video_script.substitution: Wrap a new L shaped layer around the grid so far, and each new layer has two more dots.
video_script.anchor: a square grid of six rows and six columns of dots, with the corner at the bottom left
video_script.wrong_answer: the grid is cut into equal rows
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says the grid is cut into equal rows. Equal rows would hold six dots each time, but the parts must hold one, three, five and so on, so the parts must change size, and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The grid is cut into nested L shaped layers

final_answer.value: Cut the grid into nested L-shaped layers with 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 dots from one corner outwards.
final_answer.spoken: the grid is cut into nested L shaped layers

hold_back: The grid is cut into nested L shaped layers
never_show: the grid is cut into equal rows
maths_rules: start at one corner with 1 dot
wrap an L shape of 3 dots around it: 1 + 3 = 4 dots
wrap an L shape of 5 dots around that: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 dots
each new L shape has 2 more dots than the one before: 7, 9, 11
slip: equal rows would hold 6 dots each, not 1, 3, 5
video_script.design: One idea: cut the grid into nested L shaped layers from one corner. Assumes square grids of dots. Wrong idea: the grid is cut into equal rows. The grid stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a square grid of 6 rows and 6 columns of dots, with the numbers 1, 3, 5, 7 written beside it

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.grid: the square grid of dots appears
marks.ask: the numbers one, three, five and seven appear beside the grid

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a square grid of dots.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>The grid has six rows, and each row has six dots.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we cut the dots into parts of one, three, five, seven and so on?

beats.on_screen: the grid holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: one row and one column of dots drawn from a shared corner dot, outlined as a corner shape

marks.corner: a row and a column of dots appear, sharing one corner dot
marks.shape: the two lines are outlined together as one corner shape

narration: <bookmark mark='corner'/>A row and a column of dots can share one corner dot.
<bookmark mark='shape'/>Together they make a corner shape that looks like the letter L.

beats.on_screen: Given: a square grid of dots, parts of 1, 3, 5, 7, ... dots
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a square grid of dots, and parts of one, three, five, seven and more dots.

beats.on_screen: To find: how to cut the grid into these parts

marks.find: the words how to cut the grid are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find a way to cut the grid into these parts.

marks.dot: the bottom left dot of the grid is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='dot'/>Step one, start at one corner. Circle that single dot, which is the first part with one dot.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, wrap an L shape of 3 dots around it: 1 + 3 = 4 dots

marks.three: an L shape of three dots is outlined around the corner dot
marks.four: the sum 1 + 3 = 4 is written and the four dots form a two by two square

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, wrap an L shape of three dots around it.
<bookmark mark='four'/>One plus three is four dots, and they fill a two by two square.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, wrap an L shape of 5 dots around that: 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 dots

marks.five: an L shape of five dots is outlined around the two by two square
marks.nine: the sum 1 + 3 + 5 = 9 is written and the nine dots form a three by three square

carries_over: the L shape of three dots
narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step three, wrap an L shape of five dots around that square.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>One plus three plus five is nine dots, and they fill a three by three square.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, keep going: each new L shape has 2 more dots: 7, 9, 11, and 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 36

marks.more: L shapes of seven, nine and eleven dots are outlined one after another
marks.all: the whole grid is covered and the sum 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 = 36 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='more'/>Step four, keep going. Each new L shape has two more dots than the one before. We get seven, nine and eleven.
<bookmark mark='all'/>The six layers cover the whole grid of thirty six dots.

beats.on_screen: Answer: The grid is cut into nested L shaped layers
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The grid is cut into nested L shaped layers, with one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven dots.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the grid with its first row outlined and 6 written beside it, then the L shape of 3 outlined; the bubble is struck through

marks.rows: the first row is outlined and six is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the grid is cut into equal rows.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>But equal rows would hold six dots each time. We need parts of one, three and five dots.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The parts must change size, and the L shapes do that.
